items.article: Leigh was strength training four times a week, walking 10K steps a day, yet the scales kept climbing. After doctors repeatedly told her to exercise more, a shocking photo forced her to search for answers. For a long time, Leigh Woods avoided paying too much attention to her reflection. At 110kg, she didn't particularly like looking at herself in the mirror and had become good at avoiding it. Then she spotted a side-on photograph of herself in a workplace newsletter. 'I was just like, "Oh, is that what I look like? I need to do something about it,"' the 35-year-old, from Sydney , tells the Daily Mail. By then, Leigh's confidence had taken a hit. She was going out less and didn't particularly want to be seen. Even her motivation was beginning to suffer, although she was still getting herself to the gym. That was the part she couldn't understand. Leigh wasn't someone who had stopped exercising as her weight climbed. She was strength training four mornings a week, aiming for 10,000 steps a day and fitting in cardio sessions, while also paying attention to her nutrition. Yet she estimates she was gaining around 10kg a year. After years of trying to shift it, Leigh had started wondering whether the problem was her. items.article: Christa Pike, 50, was an accomplice in a murder she committed at 18 of Colleen Slemmer. She was due to be the first woman executed by the state in more than 200 years. Christa Pike, 50, remains in a hospital early Thursday after a botched execution in Tennessee. Pike, the lone woman on death row, was set to be the first female in more than 200 years the state had put to death, according to historical records . However, after she was injected twice with a lethal drug, Pike did not die, and she was transferred to an “off-site medical facility,” a spokesperson for the Department of Correction told NBC News. Attorneys for Pike said late Wednesday that she was being treated at a hospital but that they did not know her condition. In 1995, Knoxville police said Pike and two teenage accomplices had worked together to torture, slash and fatally beat Colleen Slemmer, 19. Police said Pike and the others lured Slemmer, a classmate in their Job Corps training program, to an abandoned steam plant at the nearby University of Tennessee and attacked her. The case became sensationalized when investigators said it was tied to the occult because someone had carved a pentagram into Slemmer’s chest and Pike bragged to another student that she had kept a fragment of the victim’s skull as a “souvenir.”

He hosts the Jokes on News podcast with his former Late Show colleagues Steve Waltien, Eliana Kwartler, Michael Cruz and Kayne. items.text: Is a 'fantasy' now driving Australia's power reliability outlook?
items.article: Historically, forecasting power reliability was a sober task. Experts say Australia is now counting on projects that will never be built. In the chaos and complexity of energy in Australia, one topic has always cut through the noise: blackouts. Or, more precisely, the need to avoid blackouts at seemingly any cost, so untenable are the political consequences. It is for this reason that so much of Australia's energy planning goes towards making sure there is always enough capacity to keep the lights on. "When people say, 'Oh, we've breached the reliability standard, therefore blackouts', the reliability standard that we have is incredibly, incredibly tight," Tristan Edis of Green Energy Markets says. To be exact, Australia's "reliability standard" prescribes that consumers should expect their electricity needs to be met 99.998 per cent of the time. In other, albeit simplified, words, no more than 0.002 per cent — or 10 minutes — of their demand should go unserved across an entire year.

items.article: Heimir Hallgrímsson may be on to something in reuniting Parrott with Adam Idah up front In the privacy of Ireland ’s team room at the Castleknock Hotel ahead of the World Cup playoff against the Czech Republic in March, Heimir Hallgrímsson hung a series of giant images from the delirious 3-2 victory over Hungary on the walls. This reporter gained access to the team room to interview Hallgrímsson, and one image that hung beside the PowerPoint screen stood out above the others. The photo was taken behind the goal as Troy Parrott scored, his face contorted in desperate effort to reach a stud to the dropping ball. It was the only image we had seen that foregrounded the desperation of his effort rather than the deftness of his touch. The picture’s focus on Parrott’s expression reinforced the message that Hallgrímsson continually preaches about his new talisman: all of this is founded on work ethic. Asked to sing another round of hosannas to Parrott after his two goals against Austria, the head coach again pointed to his striker’s less glamorous qualities. “I always say that what I see in him, what I don’t see in many other attackers, is defensive discipline and hard work for the defensive structure as well,” said Hallgrímsson. Look back closely at Parrott’s winning goal in Budapest and you’ll realise his exquisite timing in meeting Liam Scales’s knock-down was a direct consequence of his work ethic.

items.article: Experts say that if you’re eating any berry – strawberries, blackberries, currants, raspberries, blueberries – you are benefiting Sprinkled on top of yoghurt, blended into smoothies or baked into crumbles, berries are among Americans’ favorite fruits. Luckily, berries are as healthy as they are delicious and versatile: low in calories, full of vitamins and antioxidants, and a good source of fiber. Research shows that, depending on the type, berries support cardiovascular health , may boost gut health and fight inflammation and show promise as part of a “healthy dietary strategy for diabetes prevention and management”, to quote researchers . Meta-analyses also link compounds in berries with improved cognitive health. Here’s what experts say about the health benefits of berries. Berries bring a meaningful dose of antioxidants to the table. “Berries’ high polyphenol content is what we think makes them so protective” when it comes to mental processes such as memory and attention, said Maggie Moon, a registered dietitian. Polyphenols are a broad category of plant compounds; in berries, the most active and proportionally meaningful of them are anthocyanins, which also give many berries their blue, purple and red pigments.

Clothes steamers use heat and moisture rather than pressure to smooth fabric. A small onboard tank heats water into a steady flow of steam, which you run over garments while they hang. Instead of pressing fibres flat like an iron , the steam causes them to swell and relax, releasing creases without the need for an ironing board. Because the fabric isn’t pressed directly against the hot surface of an iron, steamers can be gentler on delicate materials such as silk, chiffon and wool. items.article: His party has slipped to fifth place in opinion polls, its annual conference is riven by accusations of antisemitism and he is expected to lose a by-election. John Rentoul assesses the challenge facing Zack Polanski Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. A t his first Green Party annual conference, in 2025, Zack Polanski proclaimed his ambition to replace the Labour Party as the main party of the left in Britain. It was a big claim that energised his party, and over the following months it seemed as if such an improbable revolution could actually be happening. The Greens advanced in the opinion polls to challenge the two traditional parties of government. The party peaked in April at an average of 17 per cent in the polls, just behind Labour and the Conservatives, both on 19 per cent. Over the same period, Nigel Farage’s Reform UK remained in the lead, but was losing ground, and a complete reshaping of the landscape seemed possible. Since then, the air has gone out of the Green balloon. Even before Andy Burnham became prime minister, the party’s support started to subside. Now, as the party once again meets at conference, it has just been overtaken by the Liberal Democrats . The average of the six most recent polls puts Ed Davey’s Lib Dems on 10.3 per cent and the Greens on 10.2 per cent, making them the fifth party in our five-party system. items.article: "You Can See Everything" is a shocking and funny look at Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes' life. Here's what I can share without spoiling it. My row of Alice Tully Hall was filled with reporters scribbling notes about the buzzy new Elizabeth Holmes documentary . Then, we heard the warning. "In the interest of trying to preserve a relatively spoiler-free experience for later audiences, we ask that you not film and post this conversation," said Dennis Lim, the artistic director of New York Film Festival. Lim recommended shaming anyone who recorded the chat between Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the directors of "You Can See Everything." A flock of journalists put their phones away, disappointedly. The filmmakers had reason to worry: "You Can See Everything" was one of the most shocking, revelatory, and oddly funny films I've ever seen. It was twisty and worthy of seeing with fresh eyes. So, I'm not going to spoil it for you. Lim wouldn't want me to. Here's my veiled, semi-secretive attempt to tell you what I saw. The line wrapped around the block.
